title: Access is local: plane pieces keep it
claim: Access is local: plane pieces keep it. (1) Plane matching systems: a plane signed system with as many lines as odd faces has, up to complement, exactly the perfect matchings of lines to odd faces as solutions; its heights are L-natural convex, and the access lemma of PLANAR-THEOREM A and C holds on it for every pinning. A plane knot space with Kasteleyn signs split at a point into three ports is one: the three faces at the point merge into one odd face, leaving n faces for n lines. (2) The interface lemma: splice H1 minus a line li with H2 split at a point, and remove any line M. H1 minus li forces li's points to an all-equal pair, so it acts on the cut as the point; H2 split excludes exactly the patterns that read the point consistently, so it acts as li. Hence the solutions restricted to H1's piece are those of H1 minus M or H1 minus li, and those restricted to H2's piece are H2 minus M, the point split, the point split with two ports merged, or H2 with the point re-signed. Each is a plane matching system when the closure is plane. (3) So every pinning of a six-pattern line of a plane piece by two points of that piece has access, wherever the removed line is. Checked: 301 point splits of 26 plane spaces, all matching systems, with 260,892 pinnings all of type (i) or (ii); on 14 splices the predicted restriction at all 266 piece-removal pairs, and 31,596 pinnings from inside a plane piece, all with access. Computed, not proved: 9,028 pinnings with one point outside the piece all have access; pinnings by two outside points fail only when the removal is outside too (528 of 620).
failure_conditions: A point split of a plane knot space with more or fewer odd faces than lines.
A pinning on a point split of a plane space of neither type (i) nor type (ii).
A splice and removal where the solutions restricted to a plane piece differ from the predicted system.
A pinning by two points of a plane piece, of a six-pattern line of that piece, of neither type (i) nor type (ii).
foundation_claim_scope: Knot spaces glued along one simple 3-edge cut (a splice of a knot space minus a line with a knot space split at a point), any removal, pieces whose closure is a plane knot space with Kasteleyn signs.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-03.
validation.status: proved, with each ingredient checked on point splits of 26 plane spaces and on 14 splices; no human or external review
validation.novelty: New here; plane matching heights and L-natural convexity are classical.
